name: Deep ITM Covered Call (ITM buy-write)
summary: Buy 100 shares and immediately sell a deep ITM call, creating a high-probability, low-return structure economically equivalent to a cash-secured put.

legs.strike_rule: Delta 0.70-0.85 (ITM), providing a large downside cushion

max_profit: (strike - net share cost + credit) x 100 - small, typically 1-2% per cycle, achieved if the stock stays anywhere above the strike
max_loss: (net debit paid for shares - credit) x 100 if the stock goes to zero. The cushion is large but the tail is still the full stock downside.
breakevens: share cost - credit per share, typically 8-15% below spot

greeks.delta: +100 shares minus 70-85 from the call = +15 to +30 net
greeks.theta: positive but modest (deep ITM calls hold little extrinsic)

when_to_use: When you want a high-probability, small, bond-like return with a large cushion and are happy to be called away. Note it is synthetically identical to selling a cash-secured put at the same strike - prefer whichever has the better fill and no dividend complication.
entry_rules: Own or simultaneously buy 100 shares per contract; coverage verified before order submission
Extrinsic in the short call >= 0.8% of the strike per 30 days, otherwise the return does not justify the capital
Reject if an ex-dividend date falls before expiry and the call's extrinsic is below the dividend - early assignment is then near-certain
Execute as a single net-debit buy-write order where supported, to avoid legging risk
management_rules: Close the whole structure at 60% of max profit, or at 14 DTE, whichever first
If the stock falls below the strike (call goes OTM), the position has become an ordinary covered call - switch to covered-call management rules
Do not roll a deep ITM covered call down; that realises the stock loss without improving the structure. Either close or convert
exit_rules: Close both legs at 60% of max profit or 14 DTE

NEVER-ASSIGN RULE: the short call here is ITM by design, so early assignment risk is permanently elevated. Close the structure immediately if the call's extrinsic value drops below $0.05, on the day before any ex-dividend date, or by 14:30 ET on expiration day. Absolute backstop 15:45 ET on expiry day
If assigned, the outcome is your shares sold at the strike for a small profit - the intended maximum outcome. Not a loss, but an unplanned, unlogged exit the position tracker must reconcile
assignment_risk: VERY HIGH by construction - the short call is ITM from day one. Early assignment simply produces max profit early, so economic harm is low, but it breaks the never-assign mandate and the position accounting. Treat extrinsic < $0.05 as a hard close.
buying_power: Net debit for the structure (shares minus credit). Roughly the same capital as a cash-secured put at the same strike.
liquidity_needs: Deep ITM calls are often wide; require spread <= 4% of mid and OI >= 100, or use the CSP equivalent instead.
common_mistakes: Paying the spread twice on an illiquid ITM call when a cash-secured put would have been one cheap fill; being surprised by early assignment the day before ex-dividend.
